item.title: Tupac Shakur Estate Sued by Death Row Producer Daz Dillinger Over ‘All Eyez On Me’ Royalties
item.description:
[Intro music plays]
Host: Welcome to this week's music news update. Today, we're talking about a lawsuit that's making waves in the hip-hop world. Daz Dillinger, a producer who worked with the late Tupac Shakur, is suing the rapper's estate over unpaid royalties.
[Short music transition]
Host: According to the lawsuit, Dillinger claims he's owed money for his work on over a dozen songs, including five tracks from Tupac's iconic album "All Eyez on Me". The songs include "Ambitionz az a Ridah", "Skandalouz", and "2 of Amerikaz Most Wanted". Dillinger says he was paid $91,000 in 2024, but the estate didn't provide any statements to back up the amount, and he believes there's more money owed to him.
[Short music transition]
Host: The lawsuit asks the court to force the Shakur estate to provide Dillinger with a full audit of profits and licenses from the songs he helped create. Dillinger's attorney, Bret Lewis, says he expects the matter to be resolved amicably. The Shakur estate has declined to comment on the lawsuit.
[Short music transition]
Host: This isn't Dillinger's first time in a legal battle over his work. He's been involved in several lawsuits over the years, including one with Tupac's mother, Afeni Shakur, back in 2001. We'll be keeping an eye on this case and bringing you updates as more information becomes available.
[Outro music plays]
Host: That's all for today. Thanks for tuning in to our music news update. We'll be back with more news and updates next time.
